title: T1021.007 — Remote Services: Cloud Services
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Remote Services: Cloud Services with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated attack simulation: cloud services abuse

steps.title: The phishing payoff
steps.caption: The attacker just bought cloud keys that malware stole from a developer laptop. One API call asks the cloud: who am I? The answer shows a CI user with far more permissions than it needs. The stolen key behaved like a normal admin key - no exploit was used anywhere.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Map the kingdom with the CLI
steps.caption: With working keys, the attacker asks the cloud for maps: which VMs exist, which buckets hold data, which users have power. The cloud answers politely, and every answer is one log line. Defenders who baseline normal Describe calls will notice this burst.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Remote execution without SSH
steps.caption: The attacker sends a shell command to the VM through Systems Manager. The VM never sees a login: no SSH key, no password, no port open. The SSM agent on the machine pulls the job and runs it - the only witness is one CloudTrail line.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Steal the instance role
steps.caption: Inside the VM, the attacker asks the metadata address 169.254.169.254 for the machine's cloud role. The cloud hands over temporary ASIA keys for that role. These keys work from anywhere, so the attacker can now act as the VM without the VM.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Copy the data out
steps.caption: The attacker copies the customer data bucket straight to their laptop with one sync command. The data flows from S3 to the attacker using valid keys. To the bucket it looks like a very hungry backup job.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Keep the keys warm
steps.caption: To survive a password reset, the attacker mints a brand-new access key for the same user. Even if the stolen key dies tomorrow, the new one keeps working. GuardDuty calls this persistence and raises a critical finding.
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Try to turn off the cameras
steps.caption: The attacker tries to turn off the cameras: stop the organization trail. A service control policy denies the call, so logging continues. The denial itself is a critical alert - it proves someone hostile is inside right now.
